name: Lupfen
description: Lupfen is a traditional trick-taking card game from Switzerland and Southern Germany. It is closely related to the game of 'Schafkopf' and 'Watten' but is played with a unique 36-card deck and features a distinctive auction system where players bid for the right to choose the trump suit and play solo against the other players. The game emphasizes precise card play and strategic bidding.

content.text: Lupfen is a traditional trick-taking card game from Switzerland and Southern Germany. It is closely related to the game of 'Schafkopf' and 'Watten' but is played with a unique 36-card deck and features a distinctive auction system where players bid for the right to choose the trump suit and play solo against the other players. The game emphasizes precise card play and strategic bidding.

Originated in the Alpine regions of Switzerland and Bavaria in the 19th century. It evolved from older German trick-taking games like Schafkopf and Watten, adapting to local preferences and card decks.
36-card Swiss-German deck: 6-10, Under, Ober, King, Ace in each of four suits (Acorns, Bells, Hearts, Leaves).
Each player receives 9 cards (in a 4-player game).

items.text: Three-Player Lupfen: Played with a 24-card deck (9-Ace only).
Five-Player Lupfen: Two players sit out each hand, rotating.
Ramsch: If all pass, play Ramsch where lowest score wins.
